config.title: Write a palindrome checker ignoring punctuation and case

intro.title: Write a palindrome checker ignoring punctuation and case
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a JavaScript function that checks if a given string is a palindrome, ignoring punctuation, spaces, and letter case. You will learn how to clean and normalize input strings using string methods and regular expressions. The core programming concepts involve string manipulation, array methods, and conditional logic. By the end, you'll have a practical tool that can determine if phrases like 'A man, a plan, a canal: Panama!' read the same forwards and backwards when only letters are considered.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for validating user inputs in forms, such as username or profile URL checks, where special characters and capitalization should not affect uniqueness. It's also used in search and filter features, like a dashboard that highlights palindromic entries in a data table regardless of formatting. Developers implement this to ensure data consistency in applications like content management systems, where titles or IDs might be compared for duplicates after stripping non-alphanumeric characters.

objectives: Implement a function that normalizes input strings by removing punctuation and converting to lowercase
Construct a string reversal algorithm using built-in JavaScript methods
Apply comparison logic to determine if a normalized string matches its reversed version
Initialize a user interface with input and output elements for palindrome checking
Bind event handlers to capture user input and trigger palindrome validation
Manipulate DOM elements to display validation results dynamically
Integrate string normalization, reversal, and comparison into a complete palindrome checker

steps.title: Create the main palindromeChecker function
steps.instruction: Create a function called palindromeChecker that takes one parameter named inputString and returns a boolean value. Start with an empty function body that returns false.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure the function has the correct name and parameter, and returns false.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named palindromeChecker is created with one parameter (inputString) and returns false.
successCriteria: The code contains a function named palindromeChecker with one parameter inputString that returns false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function is named palindromeChecker, takes one parameter called inputString, and returns false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or has incorrect structure. Create a function named palindromeChecker that accepts inputString and returns false.

steps.title: Clean the input string by removing non-alphanumeric characters
steps.instruction: Inside your palindromeChecker function, create a variable called cleanedString that uses the replace() method with the regex /[^A-Za-z0-9]/g to remove all non-alphanumeric characters from the inputString parameter.
steps.hint: The replace() method can take a regular expression as its first argument. Use the regex pattern /[^A-Za-z0-9]/g to match anything that's not a letter or number, and replace them with an empty string ''.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your palindromeChecker function will now have a cleanedString variable that contains only alphanumeric characters from the original input.
successCriteria: The cleanedString variable is created using replace() with the regex /[^A-Za-z0-9]/g to remove non-alphanumeric characters from inputString.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you're using the exact regex pattern /[^A-Za-z0-9]/g and calling replace() on the inputString parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanedString variable should use the replace() method with the regex /[^A-Za-z0-9]/g to remove non-alphanumeric characters from inputString.

steps.title: Convert cleaned string to lowercase
steps.instruction: Chain the .toLowerCase() method to the replace() operation from the previous step to ensure the cleanedString variable contains only lowercase characters.
steps.hint: You can chain .toLowerCase() directly after .replace() to transform the string to lowercase immediately after cleaning it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The cleanedString variable will now contain only lowercase alphanumeric characters, making the palindrome check case-insensitive.
successCriteria: The replace() method call is followed by .toLowerCase() to convert the cleaned string to lowercase.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to chain .toLowerCase() directly after .replace().
steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanedString variable should be converted to lowercase. Chain .toLowerCase() after .replace().

steps.title: Compare cleaned string with reversed string
steps.instruction: Inside your palindromeChecker function, add a return statement that compares cleanedString with reversedString using strict equality (===) and returns the boolean result.
steps.hint: You can use the strict equality operator (===) to compare two strings and return true if they are identical, false otherwise.
steps.expectedOutcome: The palindromeChecker function will now return true if the cleaned string is identical to its reversed version, false otherwise.
successCriteria: The palindromeChecker function contains a return statement that uses strict equality (===) to compare cleanedString with reversedString.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using strict equality (===) to compare the strings and returning the result directly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The comparison logic isn't quite right. Remember to use the strict equality operator (===) to compare cleanedString with reversedString and return the boolean result.

steps.title: Create test cases to verify the function
steps.instruction: Add test cases after your palindromeChecker function that call it with different strings and log the results to console.
steps.hint: Call palindromeChecker() with test strings like 'A man, a plan, a canal: Panama!' and console.log the results.
steps.expectedOutcome: After adding test cases, running the code should log true/false results in the console for various palindrome test strings.
successCriteria: Test cases are added that call palindromeChecker with at least three different strings and log the results.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some test cases, but make sure you're calling palindromeChecker() and logging the results for different types of strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test cases aren't complete. You need to call palindromeChecker() with different strings and console.log the results.

steps.title: Create a simple UI structure with input and button
steps.instruction: Create an input field for user text, a button to trigger checking, and a paragraph element to display results. Use document.createElement and appendChild to add them to the body.
steps.hint: You'll need to create three elements: an input, a button, and a paragraph. Use document.createElement for each, then append them to document.body.
steps.expectedOutcome: The page will show an empty input field, a button labeled 'Check', and an empty paragraph. No functionality yet.
successCriteria: Three elements (input, button, paragraph) are created with document.createElement and appended to the body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You created some elements, but make sure you have all three: input, button, and paragraph. Also verify they're appended to the body.
steps.feedbackWrong: The UI structure isn't complete. You need to create an input, a button, and a paragraph element, then append them to the document body.

steps.title: Get DOM references to UI elements
steps.instruction: Use document.getElementById to get references to the input, button, and result paragraph elements. Store them in variables named inputElement, checkButton, and resultElement respectively.
steps.hint: You'll need to call document.getElementById three times with the appropriate element IDs that match your HTML structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: Three variables (inputElement, checkButton, resultElement) are created that store references to the corresponding DOM elements.
successCriteria: The code includes three document.getElementById calls that correctly reference the input, button, and result paragraph elements, stored in appropriately named variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've obtained some DOM references, but you need all three: inputElement, checkButton, and resultElement. Make sure you're using document.getElementById with the correct element IDs.
steps.feedbackWrong: The DOM references aren't set up correctly. You need to use document.getElementById three times to get references to the input, button, and result paragraph elements.

steps.title: Create event handler function for button click
steps.instruction: Create a function called handleCheck that gets the value from the input element, calls palindromeChecker with that value, and updates the result paragraph text to show whether it's a palindrome or not.
steps.hint: Define a function named handleCheck that gets the input value, passes it to palindromeChecker, and sets the text content of the result paragraph based on the returned boolean.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleCheck function is defined that will process the input and display the palindrome check result.
successCriteria: The handleCheck function is created and contains logic to get input value, call palindromeChecker, and update the result paragraph.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the handleCheck function, but make sure it gets the input value, calls palindromeChecker, and updates the result paragraph with the appropriate message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleCheck function is not properly defined. Ensure you create a function named handleCheck that processes the input and updates the result display.

steps.title: Attach event listener to the button
steps.instruction: Attach a click event listener to the button that calls the handleCheck function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the addEventListener method on the button reference you already have, passing 'click' as the event type and handleCheck as the callback.
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will respond to clicks by executing the handleCheck function, completing the interactive palindrome checker.
successCriteria: A click event listener is attached to the button, calling the handleCheck function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the event listener is correctly attached to the button and calls handleCheck.
steps.feedbackWrong: The event listener isn't properly set up. Ensure you're using addEventListener on the button reference with 'click' and handleCheck.
